title: Control mapping and deployment options — Harborlight Securities intro
next_steps: Share SOC2 / ISO27001 artifact bundle and KMS whitepaper
Schedule a 1-hour private deployment deep-dive with Platform Eng team
Provision short latency benchmark using Harborlight sample payloads
action_items: Daniel Park: produce rough latency vs cost spreadsheet for their 256-token median job (due 2027-09-09)
Maya Thompson: send contract pilot language and Dedicated pricing tiers (due 2027-09-07)
Tom Ellis: compile list of legal hold / e-discovery requirements and send to Redwood (due 2027-09-10)
summary: Discovery focused on mapping Harborlight's regulatory controls to Redwood hosting options. Primary concerns: encryption key residency, audit log retention & redaction, VPC private control plane, and predictable latency for market data processing. Team agreed to pilot Dedicated nodes in US-East with KMS integration and a follow-up private deployment deep-dive.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Length: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood Solutions); Tom (CISO Harborlight), Priya (Head Cloud), Jorge (Platform Eng), Evan (Legal), Asha (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood inference team, with Daniel our SE and Rina from solutions.
[00:15] Tom: Hi, Tom Ellis, CISO Harborlight. we're mainly here to see how Redwood maps to our controls for securities data.
[00:25] Priya: Priya Nair, Head of Cloud. looking at deployment models and how KMS and networks look.
[00:32] Jorge: Jorge, platform. want to understand logging, retention, and e-discovery hooks.
[00:40] Evan: Evan, legal — e-discovery, regulatory holds are big for us.
[00:46] Asha: Asha, product, curious about latency and model versions for our trade summarization pipeline.

[01:05] Maya: Great, we'll kick off with a high level and then deep dive into keys, logs, and SLOs. feel free to stop and ask Qs.

[01:22] Daniel: Quick primer — Redwood offers a hosted API, Redwood Dedicated reserved pools, and Redwood Private which is VPC or on-prem. note, i'm gonna use shorthand — "Dedicate" sometimes in notes — apologies if nomenclature slides.

[01:45] Priya: First question: can customer-managed keys live in our AWS KMS? We need keys to never leave our control for some PII and trade secrets.

[01:57] Daniel: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer KMS integrations. For hosted we can do BYOK via a customer-managed key in their cloud but the control plane lives with Redwood — we call that the private-controlplane option in some docs. Important: for Dedicated pools we can do a VPC peering or PrivateLink and the KMS calls can be routed to your KMS.

[02:25] Tom: When you say "KMS calls routed", does Redwood ever create a copy of the key material? Our policy forbids key export.

[02:35] Daniel: We never export key material. integration is via KMIP/Cloud KMS APIs — Redwood uses envelope encryption; the root key stays in customer KMS. We can provide attestation and logs of KMS operations.

[02:58] Evan: What's your stance on key escrow? regulators sometimes want escrow for long term custody.

[03:05] Rina: We have an optional key-escrow offering for enterprise customers. it's an add-on and requires a legal agreement; we'll share the escrowing process doc. it's not default for hosted customers.

[03:25] Asha: On the data flow front — when a request comes in for summarization, what parts ever hit Redwood control plane logs with PII?

[03:36] Daniel: Good point. request bodies are logged for routing/debugging only under certain conditions. By default we do minimal logging on hosted; Dedicated/Private gives more control. We support log redaction rules and sensitive field masking at ingestion, and also offer prefix/KV cache options that avoid storing full inputs. Note: sometimes the auto transcript may read "K-V cash" — it's K-V cache for tokenizer state.

[04:10] Jorge: We need legal hold capability — ability to freeze logs for a set of tenants and export chain-of-custody. Is that possible?

[04:20] Daniel: Yes. For Dedicated and Private you can enable immutable log retention buckets with WORM settings and export via our audit export tooling. Hosted can do export but retention policies are more fixed — we can negotiate retention SLAs for enterprise contracts.

[04:45] Tom: What about redaction? Example: redact account numbers and national IDs before logs leave our network.

[04:55] Daniel: We have built-in log redaction pipelines that can apply regex rules or structured scrubbing. For strict environments, we recommend Private deployment close to your VPC then run redaction pre-ingress. We can also support field-level encryption before it hits Redwood runtime so the runtime never sees PII in clear.

[05:20] Priya: Latency — our trade summarization is latency sensitive: median payload ~256 tokens, p95 target ~200ms for inference. can Redwood meet that?

[05:34] Daniel: With Dedicated pools pinned to specific GPU types and with continuous batching disabled or set small, we can hit sub-200ms for 256 tokens on certain models. there's a tradeoff with throughput/cost: smaller batch sizes raise per-token cost. We'll run a benchmark with your sample traces.

[06:05] Jorge: What's the typical overhead for network when using Private VPC peering vs hosted API?

[06:12] Daniel: PrivateLink/VPC peering adds one round trip inside cloud provider network, negligible — 5–10ms typical. Hosted API via public endpoints may add more depending on egress paths and NAT. Also consider serializer/deserializer overheads.

[06:35] Asha: For model pinning and rollouts, we need strict versioning so we can A/B test models for risk. do you have rollout controls?

[06:45] Rina: Yes — Redwood Console supports canary deployments, percentage rollouts, and automatic fallback if quality degrades. We also tie regressions to prompt-set evals so you can gate rollouts.

[07:05] Evan: On compliance artifacts — we need SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, pen test reports, and a data processing addendum that covers EU data subjects. can you provide those?

[07:18] Maya: Absolutely. We maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 and have an artifact bundle we share under an NDA. We'll include our DPIA template and a proposed DPA with EU SCCs or applicable clauses.

[07:40] Tom: Are you doing any logging of prompt outputs that would be considered derived data? For regulatory review we need clarity on what can be reconstructed.

[07:50] Daniel: We log output tokens only when debugging or when a customer enables transcript storage. For high-sensitivity customers, we recommend disabling output capture or enabling ephemeral logs that are not persisted. Also, for audit, we can record only hashes of outputs with pointers to ephemeral storage for retrieval on legal hold.

[08:20] Priya: What's your approach to multi-region data residency for EU and APAC clients? We have subsidiaries in EU, and some European regulated data cannot leave the EU.

[08:33] Rina: For data residency we have region-locking: you can pin inference and storage to a region. Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in the target cloud region; Private deployments can be fully on-prem. For hosted, we currently offer region-specific endpoints with physical controls in those regions, but some customers prefer Dedicated for stronger guarantees.

[09:00] Jorge: For our finance teams we also need export controls: certain trade datasets tagged as embargoed must never be included in any cache or analytics. can we tag data to exclude it from caching?

[09:12] Daniel: Yes — tagging at request-level prevents caching and ensures KV cache bypass. We recommend a policy that marks those requests with a "no-cache" header. We can enforce at the routing layer.

[09:30] Tom: Are you certifying any sub-processors for logs/monitoring — e.g., do you use third-party analytics that could see raw data?

[09:40] Maya: We try to minimize sub-processors. We will disclose sub-processors in the artifact bundle. For Dedicated and Private customers you can opt to isolate telemetry to your own sinks.

[09:55] Evan: Regarding e-discovery, if there's a litigation hold, can you produce a chain of custody that includes the exact system versions and path for each record?

[10:05] Daniel: Yes — audit logs include service versions, model version, node IDs, and request IDs. We can mount those logs to an immutable store and produce exports with cryptographic checksums.

[10:28] Asha: Practically, what's the expected timeline to stand up Dedicated nodes in US-EAST and run a pilot?

[10:36] Maya: From contract signature, Dedicated posture can be provisioned in 2–4 weeks depending on capacity. Pilot with benchmarks, config, and integrations usually 3–6 weeks end-to-end. Private on-prem can take longer depending on customer infra and approval cycles.

[10:55] Priya: Any concerns with our compliance team about Secrets Manager rotation when integrated with your runtime? We rotate keys every 30 days.

[11:04] Daniel: We support automated key rotation. For envelope encryption, rotations are handled at KMS level and Redwood will pick up new CMKs as long as grants/permissions are in place. We recommend staggering rotations to avoid bursts during rolling updates.

[11:30] Jorge: On the logging retention — our default policy is 7 years for some audit logs. does Redwood allow that length? Are there cost implications?

[11:40] Rina: We can support long retention for audit logs, but for hosted we may need a contract amendment and the logs might be exported into your archive (S3/GCS) — there are storage costs. For Dedicated/Private, retention is fully configurable since it's your storage.

[12:05] Tom: We need to confirm that data deletion requests for EU data are honored. If a data subject asks for deletion, how do you reconcile with legal hold?

[12:18] Daniel: Deletion requests are honored unless there's an active legal hold. We have processes to flag records under hold and prevent deletion. We track hold scopes and provide APIs to list affected records.

[12:40] Evan: For the DPA, we need to add specific subprocessor restrictions. Can Redwood agree to pre-approval on key sub-processors?

[12:52] Maya: We can negotiate pre-approval for specific sub-processors in enterprise DPA; it's common to have a clause for notice and right to object. We'll surface the sub-processor list early.

[13:10] Asha: About quality: we need automated regression alerts if a rollout causes a drop in accuracy for our prompt set.

[13:21] Rina: Redwood Optimize hooks into your eval sets and will send alerts when quality metrics breach thresholds. You can automate rollback policies tied to those alerts.

[13:45] Jorge: Suppose we go Dedicated and later want to move to Private on-prem — how painful is migration of model versions and caches?

[13:55] Daniel: We design model artifacts to be portable; weights and quant profiles can be migrated. KV cache state is trickier — we treat cache as ephemeral and recommend re-warming. We provide migration tooling for model artifacts and configuration.

[14:25] Tom: For the privacy team, can logs be redacted at ingestion using a custom regex library we manage?

[14:36] Daniel: Yes — for Private you can run your own redaction library in front of ingress. For Dedicated we can wire a managed redaction service and accept rulesets. For hosted, we provide a managed rules engine — but customers with stricter needs prefer Private.

[14:55] Evan: Are there any single-tenant options for the control plane? Auditors sometimes want control plane isolation.

[15:05] Maya: Control plane isolation is available as part of Private and certain enterprise Dedicated contracts — we call it Private Control Plane. It requires separate tenancy and additional fees.

[15:30] Priya: Network egress — if the runtime calls external endpoints (e.g., for tools or retrieval augmentation), can we lock down egress to our proxies?

[15:40] Daniel: Yes — in Private we can restrict egress to your proxies. In Dedicated we can apply egress policies and VPC routing. Hosted has more limited egress control but still supports customer-provided proxies in many setups.

[16:05] Asha: For our pilot, we want to see three benchmarks: latency p50/p95 on your hosted baseline, Dedicated pinned GPU, and Dedicated with small batch policy. Also we want a cache-disabled test.

[16:18] Daniel: We'll run those with your payloads. I'll list the exact configs in the follow-up email and include the model names, GPU SKU, batch sizes, and expected cost per 1M tokens.

[16:40] Tom: A quick question on retention encryption at rest — do you support per-tenant encryption keys for logs?

[16:50] Rina: Yes — per-tenant keys are supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has tenant separation but uses our managed disk encryption by default; enterprise customers can opt for BYOK.

[17:10] Jorge: Are there audit hooks for our SIEM — like sending audit events to Splunk or SQS with guaranteed delivery?

[17:20] Daniel: We can stream audit events to customer sinks like Splunk, Event Hub, SQS. We also support batched export and webhooks. For guaranteed delivery we recommend pushing into your durable queue (SQS/Kinesis) under Dedicated.

[17:45] Evan: On data minimization, can we restrict logs to only record meta fields (request id, model version, timestamp) and never store inputs/outputs except hashed indices?

[17:55] Daniel: Yes. We have a "minimal-audit" profile for exactly that. Also we can store salted hashes of inputs/outputs to allow matching without storing raw data.

[18:20] Priya: Are there known SOC2 gaps for hosted that enterprise customers should watch for?

[18:30] Maya: Hosted is SOC2 Type II but certain controls customers want (like customer-managed control plane or per-tenant key escrow) are only available in Dedicated/Private. We can surface these gaps in the artifact bundle so your auditors can evaluate.

[18:52] Asha: If we decide to proceed, who will own the pilot and who are your internal stakeholders?

[19:00] Maya: I'll own the commercial pilot, Daniel will run benchmarks and Rina will help with security artifacts and integration. We'll loop in an account engineering lead if we go into procurement.

[19:18] Jorge: Regarding procurement — our purchasing team will need a model for usage caps and overage handling. Do you have committed tier language?

[19:30] Maya: Yes — Dedicated is usually committed capacity with monthly/annual commitments and overage pricing. We'll send proposed tiers.

[19:50] Evan: A legal question: for data processed for EU subjects, can Redwood sign standard contractual clauses or an EU DPA variant?

[20:00] Maya: Yes, standard SCCs or EU DPA terms can be included. We'll attach our DPA draft.

[20:20] Priya: Are you able to run a vulnerability scan from our security team against a staging Dedicated cluster?

[20:30] Daniel: Yes. We allow authenticated security scans under a safe harbor agreement. For Private we give full access. For Dedicated we coordinate scans with our infra team.

[20:48] Asha: About billing — we need per-route cost breakouts so product owners can see per-feature spend.

[20:58] Rina: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route breakdowns. For enterprise, we can add custom tagging to map to cost centers.

[21:20] Tom: I'm concerned about compromise scenarios — if a Redwood node is compromised, can we revoke keys and purge cached data quickly?

[21:30] Daniel: Yes — you can revoke keys, which immediately makes cached encrypted artifacts unreadable. We also have revoke-and-terminate workflows for Dedicated nodes and can scrub caches; we will document RTO for those operations.

[21:58] Jorge: Any limitations on model quantization or custom kernels that we should know about if moving between environments?

[22:08] Daniel: Some custom kernels require specific driver versions and are easier in Private. Quantization profiles are portable but performance characteristics may differ; we'll profile your models.

[22:30] Priya: For the pilot, who needs to be our internal approvers? Our list: Security, Legal, Platform, and Procurement. Expect about 4–6 week internal cycle.

[22:42] Maya: Understood. We'll align timelines.

[23:00] Asha: Anything else on controls we missed?

[23:06] Tom: Data residency mapping for subsidiaries and an inventory of what could be considered PII in our datasets — we'll send that.

[23:18] Evan: Also add the legal hold edge cases: cross-border holds, and how export to foreign subsidiaries is handled.

[23:30] Daniel: Noted. We'll include sample configurations for cross-border routing and geofence fallbacks.

[23:52] Maya: Recap: action items — we'll run benchmarks, send security artifacts, pricing tiers, and schedule a private deep-dive.

[24:05] Tom: Sounds good. For the benchmark please include p50/p95 numbers and cost per million tokens.

[24:20] Daniel: Will do. Also, one last note — if you have any special compliance frameworks beyond SOC2/ISO (e.g., FINRA specifics), flag them now so we can bring the right evidence.

[24:35] Evan: We have some FINRA-ish controls for trade retention and auditability. I'll mark those in the list.

[24:45] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifact bundle and schedule the deep-dive next week.

[24:54] End of recorded transcript (Remaining time used for quick Qs and off-the-record clarifications).
